market_holds: Front-expiry (Nov 13) straddle prices a 7.04% move, ATM IV 119%, against a median 5.25% over the last 7 prints, which went up only 2 times out of 7 (sealed baseline, 18:09 UTC). The 25-delta skew is -14 vol points, meaning calls are bid over puts, and put/call OI is 0.65, so options are paying for a relief rally. Spot about $383 intraday (Yahoo, 19:26 UTC), about 47% below the $723 close on 2026-06-30. The run-in comes in two parts. First a roughly 40% sector-wide drawdown from early October: LRCX -33%, KLAC -24%, SOXX -21%, AMAT -29% from 10-02 to today. It came with Lam's supply-capped guide (10-22), AMAT's own investor breakfast where it gave no WFE number (10-13, -7%), and the post-midterm AI-spend and Qualcomm rout (11-05, AMAT -13.6%). Then a +22% five-day rebound, also sector-wide: LRCX +26%, KLAC +21%, SOXX +17% from the 11-05 low. That rebound includes a Nov 9 US-China deal that extended the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension to 2027-01-10, which is AMAT-favourable because AMAT beat Lam that day (+11.4% vs +9%). Consensus (Investing.com, 2026-11-11): Q4 revenue $10.30B and EPS $4.06, slightly above the guide midpoint of $10.25B / $4.02. Q1 FY27 revenue $10.83B and EPS $4.23. Q1 is a 14-week quarter with a flagged opex step-up and a tax rate going to about 13%. FY27 EPS $18.77; EPS estimates are up 9.9% over 90 days while the stock is down 23%, so the forward P/E is about 21x. Whisper $4.20 (Earnings Whispers, 11-04). UBS expects revenue of $10.45B and a Q1 guide of $10.95B. Earnings Whispers puts bullish sentiment at 19.8%, down from 25.1% a quarter ago. The line the stock trades on is the Q1 FY27 guide and the CY27 WFE/demand language, not the Q4 beat. Peers this season beat and then traded on the guide: Lam -7% after hours on a supply-capped Dec guide and -12% next day (SOXX -6.5% that day); KLA's Dec guide was $4.7B vs $4.14B and it fell 5% next day against SOXX -8%.
view: This is a well-covered mega-cap reporting into a violently de-rated and then sharply re-rated tape, with no visible AMAT-specific datapoint the price lacks. The fundamental inputs since the last call lean constructive. TSMC signalled much higher 2027-28 capex and said 'tool inflation is real' (Oct 16). KLA guided Dec +13.5% sequentially. TEL raised its first-half forecast on 10-30 on customer capex. Lam put 2027 WFE above $200B. Memory is tight. The 14-week Q1 mechanically adds about 7% of days, and the Nov 9 US-China deal removed the nearest China tail. Against that: the industry component shortage (lead times reported at 12-24 months or more; Lam explicitly capped its guide and expects constraints into 2027) can just as easily cap AMAT's Q1 shipments. Opex steps up and the tax rate rises in Q1, which pressures the EPS guide against a $4.23 consensus. AMAT has sold off on 5 of its last 7 prints, including -5% in August on a guide that beat consensus. The +22% five-day bounce means the 'washed-out' setup is partly spent, and call skew says the street is already leaning for relief. Each side has a named mechanism and neither is shown to be missing from the price: the supply risk is in every preview, and the strong peer capex data is in rising estimates. My net is a coin flip with a slight tilt down on the stock's own reaction record and the supply cap, and a large move either way.

recommendation.reason: No mechanism clears the bar. Peer capex data and the 14-week quarter argue for a Q1 guide above the $10.83B consensus, but the industry component shortage that capped Lam's guide argues the other way, and both are in every preview. After a -47% drawdown and a +22% five-day bounce, the reaction will turn on guide tone and supply language I cannot see in advance. The stock's 2-of-7 up record is the only lean, and it is too weak to bet on.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A Q1 FY27 revenue guide of about $11B or more, with management saying supply does not constrain shipments, would make up the likely outcome. A guide at or below $10.8B, or an explicit supply-constraint caveat like Lam's, would make a drop likely.

self_critique: The case for long is real. The stock is at 21x forward on rising estimates, sentiment sits at a multi-quarter low, and KLA's +13.5% sequential guide, TSMC's capex raise and the 14-week quarter all point to a Q1 revenue guide near $11B. The China tail was just removed. A clean guide could produce a relief move larger than 7%. Against it, the case for short is the stock's habit of selling the news, an industry supply cap one peer has already admitted to, and a five-day bounce that has already paid for some relief. I cannot rank these with evidence the price lacks, so staying near 50 is the honest answer.
approach_notes: P6's run-in decomposition helped most: it showed both the crash and the bounce were sector moves, which stopped me reading the +22% as AMAT evidence. P4 made me check whether the Q1 bar was stale, and it was not. P7's 'estimate the line from its inputs' left a genuine two-sided split here (peer capex up, supply cap down) rather than a lean.
